title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Catégories de Deuring', with section 1 'Catégories A-linéaires et o-enveloppes'. The previous page is a typescript draft of the same text titled 'Catégories de Tannaka'; the renaming is deliberate. Setting: A is a commutative ring and C, C' are A-linear categories (Hom's are A-modules, composition bilinear).

(1) External tensor product. Let o be an A-algebra acting on an object X, and P a right o-module. P⊗_o X is the object, if it exists, representing Y ↦ Hom_o(P, Hom_C(X,Y)). Dually, Hom_o(P,X) is the object representing Y ↦ Hom_o(P, Hom_C(Y,X)). For P projective of finite type, P⊗_o X ≅ Hom_o(P̌, X) with P̌ the dual. In modern enriched-category language these are tensors (weighted colimits) and cotensors (weighted limits) of X by P.

(2) Admissible functors. An A-linear functor F is 'admissible', or 'compatible with external tensor product', if whenever P⊗_o X exists in C, P⊗_o F(X) exists in C' and the canonical map P⊗_o F(X) → F(P⊗_o X) is an isomorphism. The margin defines the dual notion 'coadmissible': compatible with Hom_o(P,−).

(3) Deuring categories. C is a Deuring category if there is an object X, with o = End_C(X), such that every object is P⊗_o X with P in P(o/A). Here P(o/A) is the category of right o-modules that are locally on S = Spec A free of rank 1, i.e. invertible / locally principal o-modules.
- In that case admissibility need only be tested on X and such P.
- F ↦ F(X) identifies Hom_{A-adm}(C,C') with the full subcategory of Mod(o,C'): objects X' of C' with an A-linear o-action such that P⊗_o X' exists for all P in P(o/A).
- In general the category of admissible functors is A-linear.

The handwritten additions generalise from invertible to arbitrary projective modules. If C has a 'strict generator' X (every object is P⊗_o X with P projective of finite type), then P ↦ P⊗_o X ≅ Hom_o(P̌, X) is an equivalence from finitely generated projective right o-modules onto C. This is Morita theory.

(4) Enveloping category. Let C(1) = Hom_{A-(co)adm}(C^op, Mod(A)); 'adm' is struck and 'coadm' added in the margin. The Yoneda functor i: C → C(1), X ↦ Hom_C(−,X), is fully faithful. The next page cuts out C_sp(1), the functors with values projective of finite type. Given a strict generator X, it identifies C_sp(1) with f.g. projective right o-modules, calling it the 'pseudo-saturé' (the o-envelope). This is the Karoubi (Cauchy) completion of C.

Purpose. In the 1965 'Galois theory of motives', this is an axiomatic Morita/Deuring framework. The name 'Deuring' points to the Deuring correspondence and the Serre tensor construction: for E an elliptic curve with o = End(E) (e.g. a maximal quaternion order for supersingular E), curves E' correspond to invertible o-modules via E' = P⊗_o E, P = Hom(E,E'). Grothendieck abstracts this to A-linear categories generated by one object with invertible twists, as a non-commutative counterpart to 'Tannaka' categories.
errors: Typo in the original: 'les Hom dans A' should read 'les Hom dans C'.

For P projective of finite type, P⊗_o X is an absolute colimit (built from finite sums and an idempotent splitting). So every A-linear functor preserves it whenever it exists; admissibility is automatic for projective P. The only genuine content for P in P(o/A) is the existence of P⊗_o F(X) in C', which follows anyway from F(P⊗_o X). The 'il suffit' reduction is therefore essentially vacuous for functors coming from C. Admissibility is a real condition only for non-projective P, which the page does not discuss.

The essential-image description (X' with P⊗_o X' existing for invertible P) is correct only if a Deuring category is defined so that all objects are twists by invertible P. Under the handwritten 'strict generator' hypothesis (all f.g. projective P), existence must be required for all f.g. projective P. Invertible P do not cover e.g. P = eo for a nontrivial idempotent e when o = A×A. The text slides between the two hypotheses.
The final sentence ('Si X est un objet de C tel que ...') is left syntactically incomplete; it continues on the next page.

ideas.what: External tensor P⊗_o X of an object with an o-action by a right o-module, defined by representability, and its identification with Hom_o(P̌,X) for P projective of finite type
ideas.modern_name: Tensors/cotensors (weighted colimits/limits) in Ab- or A-enriched categories; Serre tensor construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (tensor construction for abelian varieties, 1960s); Kelly, Street (enriched weighted colimits, 1970s–80s)
ideas.where_published: Similar module-tensor operations appear in SGA-era writing and in Saavedra's Catégories tannakiennes (1972); exact source unsure

ideas.what: Admissible / coadmissible functors: A-linear functors commuting with external tensors / Homs by modules
ideas.modern_name: Functors preserving weighted colimits (tensors); for f.g. projective weights these are absolute and preserved by all functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Street, 'Absolute colimits in enriched categories' (1983); Kelly

ideas.what: Deuring category: A-linear category in which every object is P⊗_o X for one X, o = End(X), P invertible (locally free rank 1 over Spec A)
ideas.modern_name: Categorical form of the Deuring correspondence / Serre tensor construction; Morita equivalence with invertible o-modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for elliptic curves; Serre tensor construction; Waterhouse (1969); Jordan–Keeton–Poonen–Rains–Shepherd-Barron–Tate (2018) for equivalences of abelian varieties isogenous to E^n with o-modules

ideas.what: Admissible functors C → C' equivalent to o-module objects X' in C' (Hom_adm(C,C') ≃ Mod(o,C') with existence conditions)
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Watts / Morita-type universal property of proj(o)

ideas.what: Strict generator X: every object is P⊗_o X with P f.g. projective, giving C ≃ proj(o)
Yoneda embedding into A-linear (co)admissible presheaves C(1), and the subcategory C_sp(1) of projective-valued presheaves as an envelope ('pseudo-saturé')
ideas.modern_name: Karoubi envelope / Cauchy completion of an Ab-enriched category
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-abelian (Karoubian) envelope used in Grothendieck's motive constructions (Manin 1968, Demazure, Kleiman); 'pseudo-saturé' term unsure

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck abstracted the Deuring correspondence / Serre tensor construction into a general notion of 'catégorie de Deuring'. This is an A-linear category generated by one object X with all objects of the form P⊗_o X for invertible o-modules P. He placed it beside 'catégories de Tannaka' in the Galois theory of motives, with a universal property for functors out of it. Later the literature proved such equivalences case by case for abelian varieties (Waterhouse, Kani, JKPRS 2018) without this categorical/motivic framing or credit to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Si C est une catégorie de Deuring, alors il suffit de poser cette condition pour un objet fixé X de C, et pour o = End_C(X), P un module ∈ P(o/A) = catégorie des o-modules à droite qui sont localement sur S=Spec(A) libres de rang 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a 'non-commutative' counterpart to Tannakian formalism for motives with large endomorphism algebras, e.g. CM or supersingular motives. Isomorphism classes in a motivic Deuring category would be classified by class sets of locally free o-modules, generalising the Deuring mass formula setting to motives.

missed.claim: The dual notion of 'coadmissible' functors (compatible with Hom_o(P,−)) and the precise definition of the envelope C(1) with coadmissibility are only sketched in margins. The relation between admissibility for non-projective P and the Deuring structure is never worked out.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor; it is essentially subsumed by enriched weighted (co)limits and Cauchy completion theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is Morita theory and Karoubi/Cauchy completion in A-linear language, all standard. The notable point is the explicit naming and axiomatisation of 'Deuring categories' (invertible-module twists of a single object) inside the 1965 motivic Galois theory notes, deliberately renamed from 'Tannaka'. That is a categorical framing of the Deuring correspondence not attested in Grothendieck's published texts. It is not deep mathematically.
transcription_corrections: The original typescript indeed reads 'les Hom dans A' (a typo for 'dans C'); not a transcription error.
In C(1) = Hom_{A-adm}(C^o, Mod(A)) the subscript 'adm' is struck through, and 'coadm' is written in the left margin. The intended reading is probably Hom_{A-coadm}(C^o, Mod(A)).

Left handwritten margin reads approximately: 'il suffit que C admette un "générateur strict" X i.e. tel que tout objet de C de la forme P⊗_oX avec P projectif de type fini, alors P ↦ P⊗_oX (qui est défini par P⊗_oX ≃ Hom_o(P̌,X))'. The annotation above the displayed map reads 'P⊗_oX ≃ Hom_o(P̌, X)'.
Section title correction: '⊗-enveloppes' corrected by hand to 'o-enveloppes' (o = the algebra), as the transcription indicates.
'tels que P⊗_oX' exist' — 'exist' is a typo for 'existe' in the original.
